item.text: {"text":"Recent evidence supports ranking-focused diagnostics, but does not establish that probe improvements reliably predict intervention gains. A 2024 sequential-recommendation study comparing six negative-sampling approaches across three datasets and repeated runs found that aggregate accuracy concealed head/mid/tail differences; sampler benefits depended on dataset popularity structure ([Prakash et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276)). Another 2024 paper demonstrated benefits from correcting negative-sampling bias in rank estimates ([Subbiah et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.06371)). Foundational analysis shows sampled ranking metrics can disagree with exact metrics, including model ordering ([Krichene and Rendle](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.02263)). Consequently, gains against 99 random negatives cannot establish better full-catalog retrieval.\n\nSuggested protocol—an inference from this evidence: create diagnostic holdouts solely within public training histories, withholding suffix interactions and fitting audit models on preceding prefixes. Compare fixed uniform candidates, popularity-matched candidates, model-mined hard candidates, and full-catalog unseen-item ranks on a bounded user subset. Unobserved candidates are not confirmed dislikes. Report target rank, HR@10, and target-versus-negative score margins by category, training-only item-popularity band, and history length. Predeclare probe-to-intervention hypotheses; across a small intervention set, test whether predicted improvements agree with actual category and macro HR@10 changes. Estimate paired uncertainty by resampling the same users for both models within each category, then averaging the four category differences; cluster repeated prefixes by user. Bootstrap intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty, not training-seed variability or adaptive-search bias. Keep these audits auxiliary: preserve the pinned host evaluator, seeds, splits, and equal category weighting; reserve limited host-validation checks for shortlisted interventions. Diagnostic validity requires demonstrated intervention gains, not merely plausible probe scores."}
